description_en: The construction of the Śiva temple in the year 1887 CE (VS 1944) is attributed to Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera.This temple, named Vīrarājabhakteśvara, is one of the three Śiva temples built by Vīra Śamśera within the Pandhra Śivālaya complex. Found on the eastern bank of the Bagmati river, opposite the cremation grounds, the complex comprises fifteen similar shrines dedicated to Śiva, all linked to Jaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā. Positioned to the south of Vīramāyābhakteśvara (PPK0323), this temple is not officially part of the Pandhra Śivālaya ensemble but shares architectural similarities with them.Constructed from stone, Vīrarājabhakteśvara showcases a bell-shaped roof crowned with a metallic finial. Accessible from all directions, each entrance contains a stone archway (toraṇa) adorned with a central carving of Chepu, a mythical water creature. The southern entrance is recognized as the primary access point to the inner sanctum.Within the sanctum, a central stoneśivaliṅgarepresents Vīrarājabhakteśvara Mahādeva, the main deity of the temple. Although the temple may house statues of four other deities following the Śiva Pāñcāyana concept, this cannot be confirmed as its sanctum remains closed most of the time. Meanwhile, a Bhairava mask is embedded in the southern outer wall, and a statue of Nandī, the animal mount of Śiva, is positioned in front of the western entrance. Additionally, a statue of Kāmadeva is established on the eastern side of the temple’s plinth.Prime Minister Vīra Śamśera erected the temple in 1887 CE (VS 1944) (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 344; Michaels and Tandon 2017, p. 62). He undertook this construction after assuming power by assassinating the incumbent Prime Minister Raṇa Uddīpa Siṃha, who also happened to be his uncle. The construction of the temple served as his effort to showcase his effectiveness in governance following a tumultuous change in leadership (temple priest, Ghimire, male, age 55). Vīra Śamśera had also offered a bell after building the temple, but unfortunately, it has already been stolen.A Brahmin from the Ghimire caste conducts daily rituals at the temple, as well as at two other Śiva temples, Vīramadhuprakāśeśvara (PPK0322) and Vīramāyābhakteśvara (PPK0323), both also established by Vīra Śamśera. In return for his priestly services, he receives an annual sum of NRs. 10,000 from the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna (temple priest, Ghimire, male, age 55).
description_ne: प्रधानमन्त्री वीरशमशेरले विसं १९४४ (सन् १८८७) मा यो शिवालय निर्माण गरेका थिए ।पशुपति क्षेत्रमा आर्यघाटको पूर्वतिर बागमती नदीपारि पन्ध्रशिवालय परिसरको पूर्वमा वीरशमशेरले बनाएका तीनवटा शिवालय रहेका छन् । ती तीनवटा शिवालयमध्ये वीरराजभक्तेश्वर पनि एक हो । वीरमायाभक्तेश्वर (PPK0323) को दक्षिणमा यो शिवालय अवस्थि छ । घण्टाकार शैलीको यो शिवालयमा धातुको गजूर राखिएको छ । ढुङ्गाको यस शिवालयमा चार दिशामा चारवटा ढुङ्गाका द्वार बनाइएका छन् । चारै द्वारमाथि छेपु अङ्कित ढुङ्गाका तोरणहरू राखिएका छन् । दक्षिणाभिमुख द्वार प्रयोग गरी शिवालयभित्र प्रवेश गरिन्छ । गर्भगृहभित्र वीरराजभक्तेश्वर शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको छ । शिवालयको ढोका नखोलिने हुनाले गर्भगृहभित्र कुनकुन देवता स्थापना गरिएका छन् भनेर जान्न सकिएन । शिवालयको दक्षिणपट्टिको भित्तामा भैरवको मुखाकृति र पश्चिमपट्टिको पेटीमा नन्दी स्थापना गरिएको छ । शिवालयको पूर्वपट्टि रहेको पेटीमा कामदेव स्थापना गरिएको छ ।प्रधानमन्त्री वीरशमशेरले विसं १९४४ (सन् १८८७) मा यो शिवालय निर्माण गरेका थिए (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.344; Michaels and Tandon 2017, p.62) । विसं १९४२ (सन् १८८५) मा रणोद्दीपसिंहको हत्या गरी सत्तामा आएपछि आफूले सुचारुपूर्वक राजकाज चलाइरहेको प्रतीक स्वरूप वीरशमशेरले यो शिवालय निर्माण गरी दक्षिणमा घण्टा पनि चढाएका थिए (Priest of the śivālaya from a Ghimire caste, male, age 55) । तर अहिले उक्त घण्टा चोरी भइसकेको छ ।यो शिवालयमा घिमिरे थरका ब्राह्मणलाई पुजारीको रूपमा नियुक्त गरिएको छ । उनलाई वीरराजभक्तेश्वर लगायत वीरशमशेरले बनाएका अन्य दुई शिवालय वीरमधुप्रकाशेश्वर (PPK0322) र वीरमायाभक्तेश्वर (PPK0323) मा पनि नित्यपूजा गर्ने जिम्मेवारी दिइएको छ । तीनवटै शिवालयमा पूजा गरेवापत् गुठी संस्थानले उनलाई वार्षिक १० हजार रुपैयाँ पारिश्रमिक दिने गरेको छ (Priest of the śivālaya from a Ghimire caste, male, age 55) ।
